hero.headline: Trump to appear on Meet the Press as midterms approach
hero.teaser: President Trump will sit for an interview on NBC following a week of low approval ratings and tensions with Senate Republicans.
hero.body:
President Trump is scheduled to appear on NBC's Meet the Press on Sunday following a turbulent week that included new lows in his approval ratings and growing tensions with Senate Republicans. The disputes have become increasingly public as the 2026 midterm elections draw closer.

The president faces mounting political pressure on key issues including the economy. His interview comes at a time when Republican lawmakers have begun to voice concerns more openly about the administration's direction. The appearance represents an opportunity for Trump to address both internal party tensions and broader policy questions ahead of the midterms.

cards.headline: Iran launches missiles and drones toward Strait of Hormuz as peace talks stall
cards.body:
Iran fired ballistic missiles and drones at Kuwait and Bahrain on Saturday, escalating tensions after the US military shot down Iranian drones and struck radar installations in the region. The attacks represent the latest in a series of tit-for-tat exchanges that threaten to unravel an already fragile ceasefire agreement between Washington and Tehran.

Air raid sirens sounded across Bahrain as residents were instructed to move to safe locations. Kuwait's military confirmed it was intercepting drones and missiles launched at the country. The Iranian Revolutionary Guard Corps said it was targeting the Ali al-Salem airbase in Bahrain, where the US Navy's 5th Fleet is headquartered.

The escalation began when US Central Command announced it had shot down four Iranian attack drones headed toward the Strait of Hormuz, describing them as posing "an immediate threat to regional maritime traffic." The US military also struck Iranian coastal radar sites on Sirik and Qeshm Island in what it characterized as a defensive measure "to defend against further attacks."

Hours later, Iran responded with its own strikes. The Iranian military said it fired seven ballistic missiles toward Kuwait and Bahrain. Central Command reported that six were intercepted and one failed to reach its target. The command denied Iranian claims that the strikes damaged the 5th Fleet headquarters, stating there were no reports of harm to US personnel.

The Strait of Hormuz remains a critical global chokepoint through which roughly one-fifth of the world's oil supplies transit. The ongoing military confrontations in the region have sent energy prices spiking and disrupted global supply chains. The US military is enforcing a blockade on Iranian ports in response to Iran's restrictions on shipping through the strait.

The World Food Programme warned that millions of people face increased hunger due to the conflict's effects, primarily from soaring energy and food prices. Analysts say the war has extended regional instability and thrown the global economy into disarray.

President Trump told reporters on Friday that "the situation with Iran seems to be going quite well," despite the continued military exchanges. He predicted the administration would "come out of Iran very quickly" and promised that fertilizer prices would decline. Trump attributed the slow progress in negotiations to the difficulty of the situation for Iran, saying the country faced demands "they never thought they'd be doing."

US and Iranian negotiators have spent weeks attempting to extend the ceasefire by 60 days and initiate new discussions on Iran's nuclear program. However, both sides continue demanding changes to any agreement, with neither appearing willing to compromise significantly. The repeated cycles of military strikes undermine diplomatic efforts to achieve a lasting resolution to the conflict.

cards.headline: Ukraine launches mass drone strikes on St. Petersburg after Putin rejects talks
cards.teaser: Ukrainian forces unleashed hundreds of drones targeting Russian military facilities in St. Petersburg after President Putin rejected a proposed meeting with President Zelenskyy.
cards.body:
Ukrainian forces conducted extensive drone attacks on St. Petersburg, disrupting Russia's economic forum. The strikes targeted military installations in the city and produced visible plumes of smoke that overshadowed the flagship event meant to demonstrate Russia's economic strength.

The attacks followed Putin's rejection of a proposed meeting with Zelenskyy. In response, the Ukrainian leader is now attending talks in London with UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer, French President Emmanuel Macron, and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz to discuss continued support for Ukraine.

cards.headline: Chinese President Xi Jinping to visit North Korea as Pyongyang reaffirms nuclear status
cards.teaser: Chinese President Xi Jinping will make a rare visit to North Korea, a day after Pyongyang called US denuclearization efforts an anachronistic dream.
cards.body:
Chinese President Xi Jinping will travel to North Korea next week in his first visit since 2019. Both countries announced the trip on Friday, a day after North Korea unveiled a new facility for producing nuclear fuel.

North Korea has reaffirmed its status as a nuclear power, dismissing US efforts to achieve denuclearization as an "anachronistic dream." The timing of Xi's visit alongside Pyongyang's nuclear declaration suggests coordination between China and North Korea ahead of potential negotiations with Washington.

cards.headline: US weighs transferring frozen Iranian assets to Gulf allies for war damage repairs
cards.teaser: The United States is considering using frozen Iranian assets to compensate Gulf allies for damage caused by Iranian attacks during the ongoing conflict.
cards.body:
The US Treasury Department is developing plans to make frozen Iranian assets available to Gulf allies to help cover the costs of repairing damage from Iranian strikes. Multiple Gulf states suffered infrastructure damage during Iranian attacks, and Washington is exploring ways to support reconstruction efforts without direct American expenditure.

The proposal would redirect assets frozen under sanctions against Iran toward compensation for affected countries. Officials view the move as a way to both support allies and impose additional financial costs on Iran for its military actions. The plan has not been finalized, and details about the total value of assets that could be transferred remain under discussion.

cards.headline: Ebola outbreak spreads in East Africa as US aid role uncertain
cards.teaser: An Ebola outbreak is spreading across East Africa as questions arise about whether China will fill a gap left by reduced US involvement in global health efforts.
cards.body:
An Ebola outbreak in Central Africa could potentially reach the scale of the devastating 2014-2016 West African epidemic that killed more than 11,000 people. Modeling by the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention projects between 10,000 and more than 20,000 cases, though experts caution that outbreak trajectories are difficult to predict with precision.

The spread comes as American engagement in global health initiatives has diminished, potentially creating space for other nations to lead response efforts. China has a history of deploying medical teams and resources to combat Ebola in Africa, positioning it as a potential contributor to containment efforts as the virus continues spreading.

cards.headline: 12 people shot near street festival in Toledo, Ohio
cards.body:
Police in Toledo, Ohio are searching for suspects after a shooting near a community festival left at least 12 people wounded on Saturday.

Two of the injured remain in critical condition, according to Toledo deputy police chief Joe Heffernan. Authorities believe the incident involved at least two people firing weapons at each other rather than a random attack on festival attendees.

The shooting occurred near the Old West End Festival. When gunfire erupted, people attending the community event fled the area. Police described the level of violence as notable for the region, with Heffernan characterizing it as "over the top" compared to typical incidents in the city.

Investigators determined that the exchange of gunfire appeared to result from conflict between two individuals. Both suspects left the scene and remain at large. Police have not yet released descriptions of the wanted individuals or announced any arrests.

The victims were transported to nearby hospitals for treatment. Beyond the two in critical condition, the extent of injuries to the other ten people shot has not been detailed.

The incident adds to a broader pattern of gun violence at public gatherings across the country. Community festivals and outdoor events have increasingly become sites of shootings, raising concerns among authorities and residents about safety at such venues.

The investigation remains ongoing as police work to identify witnesses and collect evidence from the scene. Authorities are asking anyone with information about the shooting to contact law enforcement.

The White House was briefly locked down as a precaution following a separate shooting incident near the Washington Monument on Monday involving Secret Service officers, though that incident occurred in a different location and involved different circumstances from the Toledo shooting.

cards.headline: Armenia holds election as Russia pressures pro-Western government
cards.teaser: Armenians voted in elections as Russia increases pressure on the government of Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan, who is seeking a third term despite declining domestic support.
cards.body:
Armenia held elections with incumbent Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan seeking a third term. Pashinyan's government has pursued closer ties with Europe and the West, a shift creating significant tension with Russia, which historically maintains substantial influence over the country.

The election reflects Armenia's struggle to balance its relationship with Moscow against its Western ambitions. Russia has responded to Pashinyan's pro-Western orientation with increased diplomatic and economic pressure on his government.

cards.headline: Neo-Nazi party member advances to mayoral runoff in eastern German town
cards.teaser: A candidate from a neo-Nazi party has reached a mayoral runoff election in a small eastern German town, potentially breaking a post-World War II pattern of German voters rejecting such candidates.
cards.body:
A member of a neo-Nazi party qualified for a mayoral runoff election in a town in eastern Germany, marking a potential shift in German electoral politics. Since the fall of the Third Reich, German voters have consistently rejected mayoral candidates from neo-Nazi parties.

The runoff election is scheduled for Sunday in the small town. If the candidate wins, it would represent the first time a neo-Nazi party member has been elected mayor in postwar Germany. The result is being watched closely as an indicator of far-right political strength in eastern Germany.

cards.headline: Federal probe launched into California election amid slow vote count
cards.teaser: The U.S. attorney's office in California has announced an investigation into elections as millions of ballots remain uncounted.
cards.body:
The U.S. Department of Justice sent a federal prosecutor to observe ballot processing in Los Angeles as California's vote count stretched on days after the primary election. The delay in results sparked claims of election rigging, with Donald Trump repeatedly accusing state Democrats of cheating.

State officials rejected the fraud allegations. Election experts say California's deliberate counting process is designed to protect against fraud and ensure every vote is counted accurately. The system includes multiple verifications and opportunities for voters to fix errors, which accounts for the slower pace compared to other states.

cards.headline: Trump pardons former congressman convicted of insider trading
cards.teaser: President Trump has pardoned Stephen Buyer, a former Republican congressman who was convicted of insider trading.
cards.body:
President Trump pardoned Stephen Buyer, a former Republican congressman from Indiana, who served nearly two years in prison for illegal stock trading. Buyer was convicted for making trades based on inside information obtained during his work as a consultant and lobbyist after leaving Congress. He was sentenced to 22 months in prison in 2023 and ordered to forfeit over $350,000 in illegal gains plus pay a $10,000 fine.

The pardon comes as Trump's administration publicly promotes efforts to crack down on fraud. Buyer was released in 2025 before receiving the pardon. This marks another instance of Trump using his pardon power to excuse financial crimes committed by Republicans.

cards.headline: Los Angeles mayoral race tightens as additional votes are counted
cards.teaser: Raman has closed the gap with Pratt in the Los Angeles mayoral primary as election officials continue tallying votes.
cards.body:
The race for Los Angeles mayor has tightened as more ballots are counted in the city's primary election. Pratt's initial lead over Raman has eroded with each new batch of votes tallied by election officials, bringing the two candidates closer together.

The slow count has left voters waiting for clarity on who will advance in the mayoral contest. The narrowing margin reflects the competitive nature of the race to lead the nation's second-largest city. Election officials continue processing remaining ballots as the candidates and their supporters await final results.

cards.headline: SoFi Stadium workers authorize strike ahead of World Cup
cards.teaser: Workers at SoFi Stadium in Los Angeles have voted to authorize a strike as negotiations continue before the World Cup.
cards.body:
Workers at SoFi Stadium have voted to authorize a strike ahead of World Cup matches scheduled at the venue. The authorization gives union leadership the ability to call a work stoppage if negotiations reach an impasse.

The union representing stadium workers, the hospitality group managing the Los Angeles facility, and FIFA are continuing negotiations, with talks set to resume Monday. The timing of the labor dispute coincides with preparations for one of the world's largest sporting events.

cards.headline: Defense Secretary Hegseth criticizes Europe on migration in Normandy speech
cards.teaser: U.S. Defense Secretary Hegseth used a D-Day anniversary speech to attack European migration policies.
cards.body:
Defense Secretary Hegseth delivered remarks in Normandy criticizing Europe over migration, using the language of a beach "invasion" during a speech marking 82 years since allied forces launched the D-Day operation to liberate Nazi-occupied northwestern Europe.

The speech drew attention for shifting focus from the historical anniversary to contemporary political issues around immigration and border policies, representing a departure from traditional commemorative addresses at the D-Day landing site.

cards.headline: Russian economic forum disrupted by Ukrainian drone strikes on St Petersburg
cards.teaser: Ukrainian drone attacks on St Petersburg overshadowed Russia's flagship economic event hosted by Putin.
cards.body:
President Putin's flagship economic forum in St Petersburg was overshadowed by Ukrainian drone attacks on the city during the event. The strikes targeted Russia's second-largest city while the gathering was underway, disrupting what was meant to showcase Russian economic policy and international business engagement.

The attacks demonstrated Ukraine's capacity to strike deep into Russian territory, reaching a major city during a high-profile occasion. The forum typically draws international business leaders and serves as a platform for Russia to promote economic partnerships and investment opportunities.

hero.headline: States Prepare Antitrust Lawsuit to Block Paramount Acquisition of Warner Bros.
hero.body:
Multiple US states are preparing a lawsuit to block Paramount's $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, according to sources familiar with the matter. The proposed deal would combine two major Hollywood studios and has drawn significant opposition from industry workers, competitors, and regulators.

California Attorney General Rob Bonta indicated his state is actively reviewing the merger. "Paramount/Warner Bros is not a done deal," Bonta said on social media. "These two Hollywood titans have not cleared regulatory scrutiny. The California Department of Justice has an open investigation, and we intend to be vigorous in our review." Bonta also noted he was in conversation with fellow state attorneys general about potential action.

Antitrust experts say a coordinated lawsuit by state attorneys general could pose a serious threat to the deal's completion. Bill Baer, former assistant attorney general in charge of the Department of Justice's antitrust division, told the Guardian that such a challenge "presents a real threat." However, he acknowledged it would be harder for states to prevail if the federal government approves the merger.

Alvaro Bedoya, who served on the Federal Trade Commission, said state attorneys general "definitely have a shot at stopping it if they pool their resources to make a challenge." He pointed to potential labor market effects as grounds for legal action, noting that layoffs are expected as the combined company pursues cost-cutting measures.

The merger would combine extensive film libraries, television networks, and streaming platforms. Paramount announced plans to merge HBO Max and Paramount+ streaming services, a move that could reduce competition in the marketplace. The company said it would maintain separate Warner Bros. and Paramount film studios.

The Writers Guild of America opposes the deal, stating the merger "must be blocked" because "the loss of competition would be a disaster for writers, consumers and the entire entertainment industry." US senators Elizabeth Warren and Richard Blumenthal similarly warned that the deal would allow one family to dominate American entertainment, controlling numerous media properties including CNN, CBS News, and multiple cable networks.

Paramount CEO David Ellison expressed confidence the merger would receive regulatory approval. He stated the company was "absolutely confident" the deal would "expeditiously pass regulatory muster both in the US and abroad" and that it does "not come close to hitting any of the metrics that would be problematic."

Paramount has already responded to some regulatory concerns by offering to sell children's channels to address objections from European Union regulators. The company completed at least two information requests from the Department of Justice, with the mandatory waiting period expiring in February.

The deal remains under active review by US antitrust officials, according to recent reporting.

cards.headline: SpaceX IPO Plans Face Skepticism Over $1.8 Trillion Valuation
cards.teaser: Wall Street analysts question whether SpaceX can execute a successful public offering at its proposed valuation.
cards.body:
Elon Musk's plans for a SpaceX initial public offering at a $1.8 trillion valuation are drawing skepticism from financial analysts who question whether the market can absorb such a large deal. Barron's reported the proposed IPO may be too big to succeed, while Bloomberg described Musk as dropping a boulder in a kiddie pool.

JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon hosted a SpaceX event for investors, leaving many starstruck according to Bloomberg. Yahoo Finance noted the IPO dream runs into Wall Street's oldest test of matching ambitious valuations with investor demand. The Wall Street Journal reported that other space-focused stocks exist beyond SpaceX for investors interested in the sector.

cards.headline: Bitcoin Falls to Lowest Level Since October 2024
cards.teaser: Bitcoin dropped below $60,000 in its worst weekly performance since the FTX collapse.
cards.body:
Bitcoin dropped below $60,000 this week, marking its lowest point since October 2024 and erasing all gains accumulated since November's presidential election. The decline represents the cryptocurrency's worst weekly performance since the FTX exchange collapsed in late 2022, according to CoinDesk.

Ethereum also experienced significant losses during the selloff. The broad crypto market downturn wiped out billions in bullish positions held by investors betting on price increases.

cards.headline: Eli Lilly Reports Trial Results for Next-Generation Obesity Drug
cards.teaser: The pharmaceutical company said retatrutide showed improvements in weight loss, diabetes markers, knee pain, and sleep apnea.
cards.body:
Eli Lilly released trial data showing its experimental obesity drug retatrutide drove improvements in weight loss, hemoglobin A1C levels in diabetes patients, knee osteoarthritis pain, and obstructive sleep apnea. The triple agonist drug targets three different hormone receptors involved in metabolism and appetite regulation.

Lilly shared safety and tolerability data on the medication at a diabetes conference. Reuters reported the drug demonstrated benefits for sleep apnea in addition to weight loss. The company positioned retatrutide as a next-generation treatment for obesity and related health complications.

cards.headline: Companies Invest in Training Programs for Mechanics and Electricians
cards.teaser: Major corporations are funding vocational education to address shortages in skilled trades.
cards.body:
Large US companies are spending money to create training programs for mechanics, electricians, and other skilled tradespeople to address workforce shortages. The Wall Street Journal reported businesses are investing in vocational education as demand for these workers outpaces supply.

Ford's CEO warned the blue-collar worker shortage could affect consumer costs. A TechForce report found the collision repair industry's technician pipeline fills only 42 percent of current demand. Companies are developing their own training initiatives rather than waiting for traditional educational systems to produce enough qualified workers.

cards.headline: Bank of America Adjusts Broadcom Price Target After Earnings
cards.teaser: The investment bank revised its stock price target for the semiconductor company following recent financial results.
cards.body:
Bank of America reset its price target for Broadcom following the company's earnings report. The adjustment came as the stock declined in reaction to management's conservative forward guidance.

Market analysts offered differing perspectives on the selloff. Some argued the stock drop was excessive given the actual earnings results, while others pointed to continued pressure from the cautious outlook management provided to investors.

cards.headline: Executives Deploy AI Versions of Themselves for Meetings
cards.teaser: Corporate leaders and professors are using artificial intelligence twins to handle routine communications and appointments.
cards.body:
Chief executives and Harvard professors are creating AI versions of themselves to answer questions and attend meetings. The technology represents a productivity tool that allows busy professionals to delegate routine interactions to artificial intelligence systems trained on their communication styles and knowledge.

The AI twins handle scheduling, respond to queries, and participate in certain meetings on behalf of their human counterparts. Proponents describe the technology as a time-saving innovation that frees executives for higher-priority work.

hero.headline: OpenAI releases Lockdown Mode to defend against prompt injection attacks
hero.body:
OpenAI introduced Lockdown Mode for ChatGPT, a security feature designed to protect sensitive user data from prompt injection attacks. The company announced the update as a defense measure against techniques that manipulate AI systems into revealing confidential information through carefully crafted prompts.

Prompt injection attacks exploit how language models process instructions. Attackers embed hidden commands in external content that AI systems read, potentially causing them to leak private data or ignore safety guidelines. These attacks have grown more sophisticated as AI adoption increases across industries handling sensitive information.

Lockdown Mode aims to reduce the likelihood that ChatGPT shares protected data when subjected to such attacks. The feature adds safeguards to how the system handles instructions, particularly when processing external inputs alongside user data. OpenAI acknowledged that the protection is not absolute and that ChatGPT remains potentially vulnerable to injection techniques.

The company positioned the release as part of ongoing efforts to secure AI systems for enterprise and high-stakes applications. Organizations using ChatGPT to process confidential business information, personal data, or proprietary content face risks if attackers successfully manipulate the system through injected prompts. Lockdown Mode provides an additional layer of defense for users working with sensitive material.

OpenAI did not specify the technical mechanisms behind Lockdown Mode or detail which types of injection attacks it counters most effectively. The announcement reflects broader industry concerns about AI security as language models become embedded in workflows handling private information. Security researchers have demonstrated various prompt injection techniques, prompting AI companies to develop countermeasures while acknowledging that fully preventing such attacks remains an unsolved challenge.

cards.headline: Researchers identify three-foot scorpion as largest species ever discovered
cards.teaser: Fossils from 415 million years ago reveal a scorpion species over three feet long with six-inch pincers.
cards.body:
Paleontologists examining 415-million-year-old fossils have identified the largest scorpion species ever to exist. The creature measured over three feet long with pincers spanning six inches across. The Natural History Museum presented these findings based on fossil evidence from the Devonian period.

The giant scorpion lived in ancient Britain during an era when arthropods reached extraordinary sizes. Scientists attribute this extreme growth to atmospheric conditions vastly different from today, including oxygen levels that supported massive insects like dragonflies with wingspans exceeding two feet—creatures that could not survive in our current air.

cards.headline: Shift Up announces Blood Rain as sequel to Stellar Blade
cards.teaser: The developer revealed Blood Rain, the next installment in the Stellar Blade series, with a trailer showcasing combat and urban environments.
cards.body:
Shift Up has officially revealed Blood Rain, the upcoming sequel to Stellar Blade. A reveal trailer showcased the game's fast-paced combat mechanics and expansive urban environments that build on the action style of the original.

The trailer's release generated discussion in the gaming community, with multiple outlets noting that some imagery appeared to have been created using generative AI tools.

cards.headline: Vampire Survivors developer announces Switch 2 version and studio expansion
cards.teaser: Poncle revealed a Nintendo Switch 2 version of Vampire Survivors alongside new downloadable content and the establishment of a Japan studio.
cards.body:
The developer behind Vampire Survivors announced that the game will release on Nintendo Switch 2, accompanied by new downloadable content titled Legacy of the Bloodmoon. Poncle also revealed plans to establish a studio in Japan led by Sawaki Takeyasu, creator of El Shaddai.

The announcements mark an expansion for the independent studio behind the survival game. The Nintendo Switch 2 version will bring the game to the next generation of Nintendo hardware following its success on current platforms.

cards.headline: Atari announces remaster of 2002 Godzilla fighting game
cards.teaser: Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee will return in a remastered edition launching on PlayStation 5 and other platforms this November.
cards.body:
Atari confirmed that Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee, originally released in 2002 for GameCube, will receive a remastered version arriving in November. The kaiju fighting game is set to release on PlayStation 5, with reports indicating it will also appear on Nintendo Switch 2.

The remaster brings the multiplayer brawler back more than two decades after its original release. Game Informer described it as a revival of the kaiju fighting title that featured monsters from the Godzilla franchise battling across destructible environments. Atari simultaneously announced a Barbie game collection, though details on that release were not provided.

cards.headline: Scientists removed from diabetes conference for distributing journal articles
cards.teaser: Conference organizers ejected multiple researchers, including a journal editor and former association president, for handing out reprints.
cards.body:
Organizers of a diabetes conference ejected several scientists from the event after they distributed printed copies of journal articles. Among those removed were Steven Kahn, editor-in-chief of an American Diabetes Association journal, and Desmond Schatz, a former president of the ADA.

The incident highlights tensions around information sharing at the conference, though the specific policy violations and content of the distributed materials remain unexplained by organizers.

cards.headline: New telescope survey to catalog millions of undiscovered solar system objects
cards.teaser: A facility preparing for a decade-long astronomical survey will begin operations within months to identify previously unseen objects in the solar system.
cards.body:
An astronomical facility is months away from launching a ten-year survey designed to locate millions of objects within the solar system that have never been observed. The project will systematically scan the sky to catalog asteroids, comets, and other bodies orbiting the sun.

The survey represents a major expansion in cataloging near-Earth and distant solar system objects. Astronomers expect the facility to dramatically increase the known inventory of small bodies, providing data for planetary defense efforts and solar system research over the next decade.

hero.headline: Golden Tempo wins Belmont Stakes after Kentucky Derby victory
hero.body:
Golden Tempo Completes Historic Triple Crown Victory

Golden Tempo won the 158th Belmont Stakes on Saturday at Saratoga Race Course, capturing thoroughbred racing's most prestigious achievement just five weeks after winning the Kentucky Derby. With jockey Jose Ortiz in the saddle, Golden Tempo charged down the stretch to claim victory at 6-1 odds, holding off Commandment at the finish line while favorite Renegade finished third.

The victory makes Golden Tempo only the 14th horse in history to win the Triple Crown, joining an exclusive group that includes Secretariat, American Pharoah, and most recently Justify in 2018. The win also marks a historic milestone for trainer Cherie DeVaux, who becomes the first woman to train a Triple Crown winner.

Golden Tempo's path to the Triple Crown spanned five weeks and three different distances across three states, a feat often called the most difficult achievement in American sports. The horse began its journey in May with the Kentucky Derby victory at Churchill Downs before facing what experts described as a significant pace challenge heading into the Belmont at Saratoga.

The Belmont Stakes traditionally serves as the final test of the Triple Crown, requiring horses to navigate a longer distance than either the Derby or the Preakness Stakes. Golden Tempo's performance demonstrated the stamina and speed necessary to succeed across the extended course, completing a remarkable season for the horse and its connections.

The race came before a crowd at Saratoga that witnessed a historic chapter in thoroughbred racing. Golden Tempo's victory extended a tradition of Triple Crown achievement that dates back to Sir Barton's sweep in 1919. Other notable winners in the 107-year history of the achievement include War Admiral, Whirlaway, Citation, Seattle Slew, and Affirmed.

The Triple Crown schedule typically spans five weeks, with the Kentucky Derby held first, followed by the Preakness Stakes two weeks later, and the Belmont Stakes three weeks after that. This timing structure has increasingly drawn scrutiny in recent years, as more Derby winners have chosen to skip the Preakness due to the short turnaround between races.

Golden Tempo's Triple Crown completion comes during a period of significant change in thoroughbred racing's landscape. Churchill Downs recently acquired the intellectual property rights to the Preakness Stakes in an $85 million deal, consolidating ownership of multiple Triple Crown races under one corporate entity. Industry discussions have included potential adjustments to the Triple Crown calendar, including moving the Preakness one week later to create a three-week gap between it and the Derby starting in 2027.

Despite broader challenges facing the sport, the Triple Crown remains one of American sports' most celebrated competitions, and Golden Tempo's achievement adds another legendary name to its storied history.

cards.headline: Mitch Marner scores Stanley Cup Final hat trick in Game 3
cards.teaser: Mitch Marner made NHL history with a hat trick in the second period of Stanley Cup Final Game 3.
cards.body:
Mitch Marner made NHL history during Game 3 of the Stanley Cup Final, recording the fastest hat trick ever scored in a Cup Final game. The Vegas Golden Knights were facing the Carolina Hurricanes in a high-scoring matchup that saw the Knights build a commanding four-goal lead.

The Hurricanes mounted an impressive comeback to nearly complete the upset, but Vegas held on for a 5-4 double-overtime victory. Shea Theodore sealed the win with the game-winning goal in the second overtime period, giving the Golden Knights a 2-1 series lead.

cards.headline: Nelly Korda shares US Women's Open lead as Charley Hull surges
cards.teaser: Nelly Korda shot four-under par 67 to move into a share of the lead after the third round of the US Women's Open.
cards.body:
Nelly Kord moved into a share of the lead at the US Women's Open after firing a four-under par 67 in the third round. The American maintained her position near the top of the leaderboard heading into the final day.

England's Charley Hull delivered the low round of the day with a five-under par 65, propelling herself into contention for the title. Hull's strong performance has set up a competitive finish as the tournament approaches its conclusion.

cards.headline: Gabriel Bonfim defeats Belal Muhammad at UFC Fight Night
cards.teaser: Gabriel Bonfim dominated Belal Muhammad in the main event of UFC Fight Night in Las Vegas.
cards.body:
Gabriel Bonfim secured a decisive victory over Belal Muhammad in the headlining bout of UFC Fight Night at the promotion's Apex facility in Las Vegas. Bonfim controlled the fight from start to finish to earn the win.

The UFC Vegas 118 event featured a full main card of fights. Bonfim's performance against Muhammad represented the culmination of the evening's action. The victory advances Bonfim's standing in the welterweight division.

cards.headline: Brazil defeats United States in women's soccer friendly
cards.teaser: Brazil beat the United States women's national team in an international friendly match in São Paulo.
cards.body:
The United States women's national team lost to Brazil 2-1 in a friendly match in São Paulo on Saturday. Sophia Wilson scored in her first appearance for the USWNT since 2024, but Brazil quickly answered with two goals in three minutes to secure the victory.

The match was part of the Americans' preparation for the 2027 Women's World Cup. The US had scheduled a pair of matches in Brazil as part of their World Cup cycle preparations.

cards.headline: SoFi Stadium workers authorize strike ahead of World Cup
cards.teaser: Workers at SoFi Stadium voted to authorize a strike just days before the venue hosts World Cup matches.
cards.body:
Union members at SoFi Stadium in Los Angeles have voted to authorize a strike ahead of the FIFA World Cup. The authorization gives union leadership the power to call a work stoppage if negotiations fail to produce an agreement with stadium management.

The timing creates urgency for all parties involved. SoFi Stadium will host multiple games during the tournament, including a U.S. men's national team match scheduled for the following week. Negotiations between the union, the hospitality group at the stadium, and FIFA are set to continue Monday.

cards.headline: Chase Elliott wins NASCAR pole position at Michigan
cards.teaser: Chase Elliott claimed the pole position for the NASCAR race at Michigan International Speedway.
cards.body:
Chase Elliott will lead Hendrick Motorsports to the green flag after securing the top qualifying position at Michigan International Speedway. Elliott posted the fastest lap during qualifying to earn the pole for the race.

The weekend schedule at Michigan includes qualifying and race activities. Elliott's pole position gives him track position advantage heading into the main event. Hendrick Motorsports placed multiple cars in competitive qualifying positions for the race.

hero.headline: Anthony Head, Actor Known for Buffy the Vampire Slayer and Ted Lasso, Dies at 72
hero.body:
British actor Anthony Head has died at age 72 from complications related to pneumonia, surrounded by his family. His daughters Emily and Daisy shared the news in a statement, describing it as "an honour and a privilege to be his daughters, and to have witnessed first-hand the impact both he and his work have had on so many."

Head gained international recognition for his role as Rupert Giles, the mentor and father figure to Sarah Michelle Gellar's character throughout Buffy the Vampire Slayer's seven-season run from 1997 to 2003. Sarah Michelle Gellar paid tribute on Instagram, beginning with a quote from her character: "Tell Giles I figured it out and I'm ok." She continued: "Well I don't have it figured out and I'm not ok. But I know I'm the lucky one because I knew you."

Head's career extended far beyond Buffy. Born in Camden, London, to artistic parents, he began his professional work on stage, starring in a 1978 West End revival of Godspell. Throughout the 1980s and 1990s, he performed in various theatrical productions including the original West End production of Chess in 1988 and The Rocky Horror Show in 1990. He also appeared in films including The Iron Lady and The Inbetweeners Movie.

In the early 1980s, Head sang backing vocals for the British pop group Red Box and appeared on their 1986 debut album. However, he became arguably best known in the UK and US for his role in Nescafe Gold Blend television advertisements, which featured a slow-burn romance between a British couple.

During his five years in Los Angeles filming Buffy, Head maintained a long-distance relationship with his partner Sarah and their two young daughters in England. He told the Guardian that he would travel home every three or four weeks whenever possible, spending considerable money on airfares to maintain family connections.

After Buffy concluded in 2003, Head took a recurring role in the BBC sketch show Little Britain, playing a British prime minister constantly fawned over by a flirtatious assistant played by David Walliams. He also appeared in the BBC production Merlin. More recently, he featured regularly in Ted Lasso as Rupert Mannion, a former football club owner, where he worked closely with co-creator Jason Sudeikis and earned praise for their on-screen chemistry.

His daughters emphasized that Head "loved his job very much and he always considered himself incredibly lucky to have been able to work alongside such exceptionally talented people, in such wonderful productions, across a career that spanned several decades." They concluded: "We know his legacy will live on in the shows he was a part of and in the audiences that love them."

cards.headline: Dua Lipa and Callum Turner Wed in Sicily With Elton John Performance
cards.teaser: The pop star married the actor in Sicily, with Elton John performing at the ceremony.
cards.body:
Dua Lipa and Callum Turner married in Sicily, with Elton John serenading the couple with a performance of "Your Song" during the ceremony. The wedding took place in Italy, though reports also referenced wedding events in London and Palermo.

Vogue reported on the bride's attire, describing a leather element in one of her wedding looks. The Guardian noted that the wedding in Palermo drew mixed reactions from locals, with one resident quoted as saying they could understand such attention "if it was for the pope." E! News reported that the Italian wedding included references to how the couple first met.

cards.headline: Olivia Rodrigo Debuts Duet With The Cure's Robert Smith at Primavera Sound
cards.teaser: The pop star revealed a collaboration with Robert Smith from her upcoming album during a surprise festival performance.
cards.body:
Olivia Rodrigo revealed a duet with The Cure's Robert Smith during a surprise performance at the Primavera Sound festival. The song, titled "What's Wrong With Me," will appear on Rodrigo's forthcoming album, which is set for release within a week.

Rodrigo brought Smith onstage partway through her set to premiere the collaboration. Variety described the duet as one of pop's best-kept secrets of 2026. Forbes noted that the newest song breaks a longstanding tradition for Rodrigo, though the nature of that tradition was not specified in available reports. Yahoo covered the surprise set, highlighting it among the best moments of the festival.

cards.headline: Kennedy Center Loses Lawsuit Against Musician Who Canceled Over Trump Naming Dispute
cards.teaser: A judge dismissed the Kennedy Center's lawsuit against a musician who canceled a performance after the venue's name change.
cards.body:
A judge dismissed a lawsuit brought by the Kennedy Center against musician Chuck Redd, who canceled a performance in a dispute over the venue's naming. The lawsuit stemmed from Redd's decision to cancel after the center became associated with the Trump name.

The Washington Post reported that the court ruled in favor of the musician who had canceled following the name change. ABC News noted that Redd had canceled a Christmas Eve show. The Guardian and WUSA9 both covered the dismissal, with the case drawing attention due to the intersection of arts programming and political controversy surrounding venue naming.

cards.headline: Bruce Springsteen Opens Music Center With Performance Featuring Jon Bon Jovi and Public Enemy
cards.teaser: Bruce Springsteen performed with Jon Bon Jovi and Public Enemy at his new music center in New Jersey.
cards.body:
Bruce Springsteen opened the Bruce Springsteen Center for American Music at Monmouth University with a concert featuring Jon Bon Jovi and Public Enemy. The New York Times reported on the opening, noting the presence of guitars at the center.

Rolling Stone covered the second night of the "Music America" concert series, which featured the collaboration between Springsteen, Bon Jovi, and Public Enemy. The Asbury Park Press described the performance as giving concert fans something to talk about. The center is scheduled to officially open on June 13 at Monmouth University in New Jersey.

cards.headline: Ariana Grande Begins Eternal Sunshine Tour in Oakland After Six-Year Break
cards.teaser: Ariana Grande returned to touring with her first concert in more than six years at Oakland Arena.
cards.body:
Ariana Grande returned to touring after a six-and-a-half-year hiatus, launching her Eternal Sunshine tour at Oakland Arena on Saturday night. The opening show marked her first concert performance since her previous tour concluded in 2019.

Variety covered the opening night and published the complete setlist from the performance, with a full review to follow.

cards.headline: Ye Performs in Netherlands Despite Protests Over Antisemitic Controversy
cards.teaser: The rapper performed for thousands of fans in the Netherlands after a court allowed the concerts to proceed.
cards.body:
Ye performed for thousands of fans in the Netherlands despite protests related to antisemitic controversy. A Dutch court allowed the concerts to proceed after a Jewish group attempted to stop the performances.

The Times of Israel reported that thousands attended the concert despite the controversy. Sky News covered the judge's decision to block the attempt by a Jewish group to halt the shows. AP News reported on the Dutch court's ruling allowing the rapper's concerts in the Netherlands to move forward as planned.

hero.headline: Trump to appear on Meet the Press as midterms approach
hero.teaser: President Trump will sit for an interview on NBC following a week of low approval ratings and tensions with Senate Republicans.
hero.body:
President Trump is scheduled to appear on NBC's Meet the Press on Sunday following a turbulent week that included new lows in his approval ratings and growing tensions with Senate Republicans. The disputes have become increasingly public as the 2026 midterm elections draw closer.

The president faces mounting political pressure on key issues including the economy. His interview comes at a time when Republican lawmakers have begun to voice concerns more openly about the administration's direction. The appearance represents an opportunity for Trump to address both internal party tensions and broader policy questions ahead of the midterms.

cards.headline: U.S. attorney's office launches probe into California elections
cards.teaser: Federal prosecutors in Los Angeles have opened an investigation into election fraud in California's elections.
cards.body:
The Los Angeles U.S. attorney's office announced Saturday that it has launched an investigation into election fraud in California's elections. The probe comes as vote counting continues in several key races across the state.

The announcement follows criticism from President Trump and other conservatives about California's vote-counting process. Former Speaker Kevin McCarthy echoed concerns about the process on Friday, saying California voters were losing faith as results continue to come in from the primary elections.

cards.headline: Pence says violent Jan. 6 rioters should not receive pardons
cards.teaser: Former Vice President Pence said rioters who assaulted officers or vandalized property should not be pardoned by President Trump.
cards.body:
Former Vice President Mike Pence said Friday that Jan. 6 rioters who assaulted police officers, vandalized government property, or sought to disrupt certification of the 2020 presidential election should not receive pardons from President Trump. Pence added that such individuals should never get a dime.

Pence made the comments during an interview on HBO's Real Time. His remarks come as President Trump faces pressure regarding how to handle cases related to the 2021 attack on the Capitol. Pence has been among the most prominent Republican voices opposing clemency for those involved in violence during the riot.

cards.headline: White House AI policy adviser to step down at end of month
cards.teaser: Sriram Krishnan, a senior policy adviser on artificial intelligence at the White House, announced Saturday that he will leave his position at the end of this mo.
cards.body:
Sriram Krishnan, a senior policy adviser on artificial intelligence at the White House, announced Saturday that he will leave his position at the end of this month. Krishnan, a tech investor, has been a central figure in the Trump administration's efforts to develop AI policy and strategic planning.

Krishnan played a key role in advancing President Trump's goals for artificial intelligence during his tenure. His departure comes as the administration continues to navigate policy challenges around the rapidly evolving technology sector. The White House has not yet announced who will succeed Krishnan in the role.

The timing of Krishnan's departure places the administration in a position to reassess its AI strategy heading into the second half of 2026. Artificial intelligence policy has become an increasingly important area of focus for the federal government as the technology continues to advance and raise questions about regulation, national security, and economic competitiveness.

Krishnan's background as a tech investor brought private sector expertise to the White House's approach to AI policy. His work included developing strategic frameworks intended to position the United States as a leader in AI development while addressing concerns about the technology's implications. The administration will need to fill the vacancy as it continues to shape federal AI policy in a rapidly changing technological landscape.

cards.headline: Hilton, Becerra lead early returns in California governor primary
cards.teaser: Early results show Republican Steve Hilton and Democrat Xavier Becerra ahead in the race to replace Gov. Gavin Newsom.
cards.body:
Xavier Becerra, a former Biden cabinet official, has advanced to California's general election after a remarkable turnaround. His campaign rebounded from polling near 3% in late March to secure a spot on the November ballot. If elected, Becerra would become the state's first Latino governor since 1875.

On the Republican side, Steve Hilton is leading early returns. The primary race has drawn scrutiny from federal authorities, with the U.S. Justice Department sending a federal prosecutor to observe ballot processing in Los Angeles. Vote-counting continues as mail-in ballots arrive at county election offices across the state.

cards.headline: Former Interior Secretary Deb Haaland wins New Mexico Democratic primary for governor
cards.teaser: Haaland, who served in the Biden administration, could become the first female Native American governor if elected.
cards.body:
Deb Haaland, who served as Interior Secretary in the Biden administration, won the Democratic primary for governor of New Mexico on Sunday. Haaland will now advance to the general election in November.

If elected, Haaland would make history as the first female Native American governor in the United States. She previously served as a member of Congress representing New Mexico before joining the Biden cabinet. Her primary victory positions her as the Democratic standard-bearer in a state that has leaned Democratic in recent elections.

cards.headline: Reality TV stars make waves in political races across country
cards.teaser: Spencer Pratt is in second place in the Los Angeles mayoral race, part of a broader trend of celebrities entering politics.
cards.body:
A wave of reality television personalities are running for office across the country, with several showing strength in early returns. Spencer Pratt, known for his reality TV career, is in second place in the Los Angeles mayoral race. Luke Gulbranson, another reality television star, has announced a run for office.

The trend highlights how celebrity status can help candidates gain traction even without political experience. Pratt's performance in the Los Angeles race has surprised political observers, as he advances in a competitive field. The phenomenon reflects broader changes in how voters evaluate candidates and the role of name recognition in electoral politics.
